sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

stage_1.expense_line_item: Name reservation application and RCS handling fee (through the notarial office)
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 (approx. EUR 155)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Article 26-1 et seq. (general partnership rules) and Articles 318-1 to 318-33 (Special Limited Partnership - SCSp), as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 and amended by the Law of 25 August 2015 on legal capacity; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners and the Grand-Ducal Regulation on the Trade and Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Ministry of Justice, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société (partnership agreement), being the constitutive instrument of the SCSp, deposited in electronic form with the RCS through the LBR e-incorporation portal; notarial form is required only where the SCSp opts for separate legal personality or contributes real estate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to the SCSp; the partnership agreement freely determines the amount, form and payment schedule of contributions. No escrow or blocked-account requirement is imposed under Article 318-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915; contribution payment evidence is retained in the bank file only.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1) The partnership agreement (contrat de société) establishing the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) is adopted in final form; the general partner accepts its management mandate and the limited partners subscribe the initial contributions per the capital schedule. 2) The registered office is fixed in Luxembourg. 3) The managing general partner is appointed sole representative to bind the SCSp, open bank accounts and execute contracts. 4) The managing general partner is authorised to file the deed with the RCS, register for VAT, ACD income tax and RBE, and engage Luxembourg legal, tax and audit advisers. 5) All prior acts in furtherance of incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name vetting and non-opposition certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), e-naming service at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application through the LBR naming service proposing the SCSp name and two alternates. Pay the reservation fee and receive the certificat de non-opposition, which is valid for six months and confirms that the proposed name is not confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name or trademark.
required_dossiers: Application form for reservation of a corporate name
Proposed SCSp name and two alternates
Identity document of the general partner or formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS refuses the name for confusing similarity, file a new request using the alternate names; the certificate fee is not refunded and the substitute certificate is processed within the same 3-day window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement (contrat de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notarial deed required only if the SCSp opts for legal personality or contributes real estate) or private deed signed by all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in French (an English version may be attached) containing the SCSp name, registered office in Luxembourg, general partner identity and powers, financial year, contribution schedule and profit-sharing waterfall. Have all general and limited partners sign the deed and legalise or apostille signatures where foreign partners sign outside Luxembourg. If the SCSp has opted for legal personality, execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary with certified annexes.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the partnership agreement
Passport copies and proof of address of all partners
Power of attorney for drafting counsel (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or drafting counsel identifies a statutory defect, execute an acte rectificatif before the same notary; for a private deed, re-execute a consolidated version signed by all partners before the RCS deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing and registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers eRegistre / e-incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed partnership agreement, certificate of non-opposition, Form A (powers of representation) and the general partner's consent through the LBR eRegistre platform. Pay the statutory filing fee online. The RCS examines compliance under Articles 318-1 et seq. and issues the RCS registration number and the official extract (extrait du RCS).
required_dossiers: Form A — list of managers and authorised signatories
Identity documents of the general partner
Notarial deed (if executed before a notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a formal query or suspension, remedy the deficiencies within the stated deadline, typically one month, by re-uploading corrected documents; substantive defects are cured by an acte rectificatif before re-filing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority - portal: pfi.public.lu and myguichet.lu; direct tax administration: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - portal: impotsdirects.public.lu; customs administration: Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) - portal: douanes.public.lu; business register: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - portal: lbr.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Luxembourg SCSp trading in SSD and CPU chips, the statutory sequence is: (1) execute the SCSp partnership agreement (by notarial or private deed) and file for registration with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the LBR portal, obtaining the RCS number and an 11-digit national business identification number; (2) file VAT registration Form 1040 with the AEDT electronically via myguichet.lu once the annual taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 or immediately where the SCSp makes intra-Community acquisitions exceeding EUR 10,000, imports goods, supplies goods to Luxembourg customers, or intends to claim export zero-rating and input VAT recovery; (3) obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by 8 digits; (4) register for customs purposes with the ADA to obtain an EORI number in the format LU followed by 11 digits for physical export of the semiconductor goods; (5) appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative where the SCSp is considered not established in Luxembourg and is owned by non-EU resident partners; (6) file the annual informative income tax return (Formulaire 510) with the ACD solely for partner allocation purposes, since the SCSp is fiscally transparent and carries no corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax liability at entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is transparent by statutory default under Articles 50-26 of the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies; the entity is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (IFC), or net wealth tax (IFT), and no equivalent of the US check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg domestic law; partners may structure the partnership agreement to govern profit allocation among general and limited partners; the general partner may elect to form a VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 60 LGTVA where common control exists, may elect the cash-accounting method for VAT under Article 63 LGTVA when annual turnover is below EUR 500,000, and may voluntarily waive the small-business exemption under Article 162 LGTVA to recover input VAT; hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD, as transposed by the Law of 21 December 2018, apply automatically where a foreign jurisdiction fiscally treats the SCSp as an opaque entity, and the ACD will apply the fraus legis and general anti-abuse rules under Article 6 paragraph 1 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) to disregard artificial arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Luxembourg Value Added Tax / Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) enacted by the Law of 12 February 1979 (LGTVA), transposing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover excluding VAT for the small-business exemption under Article 162 LGTVA; mandatory VAT registration is nevertheless required without any turnover threshold where the SCSp makes intra-Community acquisitions exceeding EUR 10,000, imports goods from outside the EU, engages in distance sales into Luxembourg, receives reverse-charge services, or makes any export supply for which zero-rating or input VAT recovery is claimed; the wholesale SSD and CPU chip export activity therefore triggers compulsory VAT and EORI registration irrespective of domestic turnover levels
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, API filing, or digital stamping regime; standard electronic invoicing (PDF, UBL, Factur-X, EDI) is permitted and accepted by the AEDT; recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) for intra-Community supplies must be filed online through the eSpace portal by the 15th day of the following month; Intrastat declarations for dispatches are required monthly once the annual dispatch threshold of EUR 150,000 is exceeded; Luxembourg has announced alignment with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework with mandatory structured e-invoicing for domestic B2B transactions expected no earlier than 1 January 2026, but no implementing statute, technical API, or clearance mandate has yet been enacted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of SSD and CPU chips from Luxembourg to destinations outside the EU qualify for zero-rating under Article 74 LGTVA where the SCSp or its customs agent proves dispatch or transport of the goods out of the customs territory of the EU within 90 days of the supply and holds the full export documentation trail; intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-registered EU customer qualify for zero-rating under Article 43 LGTVA provided the customer VAT number is validated through VIES, the goods are physically dispatched to another Member State, and the corresponding EC Sales List is timely filed; the zero-rate claim fails where the goods remain in Luxembourg or another EU Member State, where the transport evidence is incomplete or inconsistent with the Incoterms, where the invoiced counterparty is not the actual acquirer in a serial-resale chain, or where the SCSp cannot prove its economic substance in Luxembourg; although Luxembourg imposes no statutory exchange-control deadline, the 180-day repatriation benchmark in this dossier reflects the standard commercial settlement term in the SWIFT TT and escrow inspection wire structure and must be demonstrated by the SCSp's export ledger upon audit
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD / EXS declaration) filed in the EU Customs Trader Portal containing the export movement reference (MRN) number and confirming exit of the goods from the customs territory of the EU

International transport document evidencing dispatch: Bill of Lading (sea freight), Air Waybill (air freight), or CMR/CIM consignment note (road or rail) bearing signatures, dates, and stamps of the foreign consignee or carrier
Commercial invoice and underlying sale contract or purchase order identifying the precise SSD and CPU chip specifications, quantities, unit prices, and agreed Incoterms delivery point
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement confirmation evidencing receipt of the export proceeds on the SCSp's bank account within the contractual and tax documentation deadline
VIES validation receipt for EU intra-Community customers together with the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) filed with the AEDT
Proof of exit from the EU including customs stamps, export MRN numbers, delivery acknowledgements from the ultimate consignee, and any warehouse or free-zone movement records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may deny the zero rate and reassess VAT at 16% with statutory late interest accruing at 0.6% per month on arrears where the export documentation bundle is defective, inconsistent, or missing; administrative fines under Articles 411 to 416 LGTVA range from EUR 250 to EUR 50,000, and the tax authorities may apply assessment penalties of up to 10% of the evaded tax in cases of negligent under-declaration; fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger criminal sanctions under Article 412 LGTVA of EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years, with enhanced fines for organized fraud; the AEDT may also apply the fraus legis doctrine and the general anti-abuse provision of Article 6 paragraph 1 LIR to re-characterize artificial interposition structures involving shell partners or circular re-invoicing; retrospective clawbacks may extend to the full statutory assessment period of 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud, with joint and several liability of the general partner for the non-institutional SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Information Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle de l'inscription au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year; filing open 1 January – 31 December; mandatory confirmation due no later than 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS sends written reminder; daily coercive astreinte up to EUR 2,500; failure to respond within the additional grace period triggers judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Déclaration annuelle au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, due by 31 December; plus mandatory update within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties for the entity (up to EUR 1,250,000) and for responsible managers (imprisonment and fines); public notice of non-compliance; repeated or flagrant default may lead to court-ordered strike-off and prohibition on directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (if mandatory because the SCSp exceeds the legal size thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year end; for a calendar-year entity, no later than 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from EUR 500 to EUR 25,000; formal notices; aggravated judicial strike-off after persistent non-compliance; possible loss of the benefit of limited liability protections.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Direct Tax Return (income tax and municipal business tax declaration for transparent partnerships)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March of the subsequent year; electronically filed returns are automatically extended to 31 December of that calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment increase of up to 10%; administrative fines up to EUR 1,000 per return; risk of tax assessment on estimated income plus collection measures after 3 months of continued default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average number of full-time employees 50. Other obligations may arise if the SCSp is part of a group or is a public-interest undertaking. In all other cases, an audit is optional for an SCSp.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial registers and annual accounts, as amended); IFRS may be used for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any transfer of partnership interests in the SCSp must be recorded in the partner register and notified to the manager. The UBO register must be amended within 30 days of the transfer. Annually, the general partner or manager must confirm to the RBE that the beneficial ownership data remains accurate; the confirmation is filed electronically and must reach the register no later than 31 December. Full documentary evidence of transfers (sale agreements, stock transfer forms, valuation records) must be retained in the corporate file.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partnership Interest Transfers (Transfers of Parts)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 2,500 – EUR 5,000 per year (typical Luxembourg registered office and resident corporate agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 18,000 – EUR 35,000 for a full statutory audit if thresholds are met; EUR 4,500 – EUR 8,000 for an annual compliance review when no audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline for a taxable Luxembourg corporate entity in Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); 0% entity-level CIT for a fiscally transparent SCSp
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax or municipal business tax; qualifying corporate partners may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption on dividend and capital-gain income, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, an 80% exemption for net wealth tax on qualifying participations, and the IP tax box for qualifying intellectual property income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 500 (partnership information return for SNC, SCS and SCSp) filed through the ACD e-space / MyGuichet as part of the Luxembourg electronic tax filing system (eCDF)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 31 March following the end of the fiscal year, unless a duly justified electronic extension is granted by the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax file number, fiscal year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SCSp identification details; the SCSp itself has no separate CIT liability, but the return must still identify the partnership and its general partner

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total turnover, deductible expenses, net commercial profit, and allocation ratios to each limited and general partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must include only their allocable share of Luxembourg-source income derived through the SCSp; attach accounts and allocation schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C / Partner Details and Treaty Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Country of residence of each partner, PE indicators, and any double-taxation relief or treaty allocation claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the partner's tax residency certificate and confirm whether the partner has a permanent establishment in Luxembourg under the applicable DTA

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on assessed tax, monthly default interest at 0.6% on unpaid tax, and possible ex-officio assessment; deliberate non-filing exposes partners to criminal tax sanctions and fines

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 470 (Luxembourg corporate income tax return) filed through the ACD e-space / eCDF for non-resident corporate partners deemed to carry on business through a Luxembourg PE via the SCSp
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 March following the tax year; online extensions may be granted by the ACD to 30 June at the latest

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, RCS number, tax file number, registered address, and fiscal year-end of the corporate partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must use the Luxembourg PE file number and identify the SCSp through which the PE is exercised

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income attributable to the Luxembourg PE, including the partner's allocable share of SCSp trading profits from wholesale SSD and CPU chip sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg PE income; income not effectively connected with the Luxembourg PE is not taxable in Luxembourg

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 15 / Tax Credits and Treaty Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, and DTA relief claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach tax residency certificate and compute treaty relief in accordance with the relevant DTA; request reduced or deferred withholding through the ACD refund procedure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 10% of tax due, monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for serious non-compliance, and criminal liability for wilful false declarations

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by an SCSp because the partnership is fiscally transparent; if the SCSp were treated as a taxable corporate entity, the domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax rate would be 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and to 5% or 10% under many DTAs for portfolio shareholdings
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident partner must obtain an official Luxembourg tax residence certificate in its country of residence, file a treaty relief request with the ACD, and, for any Luxembourg withholding tax imposed on income sourced through the SCSp, apply for reduction or refund before final assessment; relief is granted against proof of beneficial ownership and substance and is subject to the treaty's limitation-on-benefits clause
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law does not impose source withholding tax on arm's-length interest or royalty payments; treaty rates are generally 0% for interest and royalties, while certain treaties provide 5% or 10% caps; anti-abuse rules may reclassify excessive or artificial payments as taxable distributions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions for the mandatory Luxembourg transfer pricing documentation file (Form 710 / Local File); Master File applies when the group's consolidated annual turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report applies when group consolidated annual turnover exceeds EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The SCSp is not subject to a Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but Luxembourg tax authorities require real economic substance under Circular LIR 50/2016 and the statutory abuse-of-law doctrine; an SCSp must maintain a Luxembourg office, local management, personnel, bank accounts, accounting records and decision-making documentation in order to obtain tax residence certificates, access treaty benefits, and prevent recharacterisation as a shell or sham entity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting wholesale SSD/CPU chip sales revenue, using fabricated rebate invoices, recording fictitious inventory losses, or misallocating income to a non-resident partner without an economic activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of the evaded tax, 10% fraud surcharge, monthly interest at 0.6%, criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000, and imprisonment of up to five years for wilful tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner may be held jointly and severally liable for the SCSp's tax debts; civil restitution, asset freezes, travel bans and imprisonment may be imposed where the director personally directed the fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SCSp without any physical office, local management, commercial activity, or real decision-making, solely to route SSD/CPU sales invoices and obtain treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reattribution of the full trading profit to the non-resident partner's home jurisdiction, retroactive taxation in Luxembourg, administrative penalties, and public strike-off proceedings for sham substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for resulting tax assessments and sanctions; the corporate veil may be pierced if directors permitted the entity to operate as a pure conduit with no economic substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Luxembourg Local File and Form 710 where cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000, or applying an unjustified mark-up on intercompany SSD/CPU chip trades
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward transfer pricing adjustment to arm's length results, double taxation, 10% documentation penalty, fines of up to EUR 50,000 for non-filing, and monthly default interest on the additional assessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the additional tax and penalties if they signed incomplete TP documentation or knowingly set artificial intercompany prices

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and UBO Violations in High-Risk Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform beneficial ownership identification, PEP screening, and transactional monitoring on Swift TT and Escrow Inspection Wire payments received from high-risk counterparties in the semiconductor wholesale market
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF/CRF administrative fines of up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for aggravated violations, suspension of the entity's right to operate, and criminal money-laundering proceedings for structured or concealed commercial receipts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner can be prosecuted personally for money laundering, face imprisonment, asset confiscation, civil damages and professional disqualification if they knowingly used the SCSp to disguise the source of SSD/CPU sale proceeds
